title: Top Noise-Cancelling Headphones for Flights & Focus (2026)
summary: The Bose QuietComfort Ultra (2nd Gen) is the best noise-cancelling headphone for most people, with the first-gen Ultra for value and the 1More SonoFlow Pro for a tight budget.
method: Picks come from Tom's Guide (updated Sep 28, 2026; every pair tested by its audio team) and TechRadar (updated Sep 21, 2026; Matt Bolton compared 17 pairs head to head with hair dryer, microwave, road traffic and busy cafe tests). The Bose QuietComfort Ultra, Sony WH-1000XM6 and Bowers & Wilkins PX7 S3 appear in both.
assumptions: Prices change often, so we quote list prices from the sources and tell you to check the current price. The two outlets differ a little: Tom's Guide ranks the Bose 2nd Gen first and puts the Sony below it, while TechRadar scored both Bose Ultra generations as joint best at blocking noise. The Marshall Monitor III is covered by Tom's Guide alone.

products.name: Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2nd Gen)
why: Tom's Guide calls the 2nd Gen Bose QuietComfort Ultra the best noise-cancelling headphones you can buy, and the best ANC it has tested. The reviewer says they make loud buses and flights far easier to bear and let them focus in libraries and cafes.
TechRadar's real-world noise tests agree: it scored joint top, level with the first-gen Ultra, and it adds a 30-hour battery (24 hours in the first gen).
specs: Active noise cancelling with a transparency mode Tom's Guide calls effortlessly impressive
Battery: 30 hours with ANC (24 hours with Immersive Audio on), per Tom's Guide
Bluetooth 5.3 with SBC, AAC and aptX Adaptive
Weighs about 250 g; both outlets list a $449 price
pros: Best noise cancelling either outlet tested
Better battery and more EQ bands than the first gen
cons: Touch controls are fiddly, per Tom's Guide

products.best_for: Frequent flyers and commuters who want the strongest noise blocking available
products.skip_if: You care more about sound quality than silence, or want to save about $100

products.name: Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (1st Gen)
why: TechRadar names these its number one pick. In its tests they tied the 2nd Gen for the top noise-cancelling score and marginally beat the Sony WH-1000XM6, especially on chaotic high-pitched noise such as a busy cafe.
TechRadar's reasoning is simple: they are often found around $300, roughly $100 to $150 below the newer models, which more than cancels out the small advantages of the new ones.

TechRadar lists a $429 list price and a $329 typical street price

products.name: Sony WH-1000XM6
why: TechRadar scored the Sony WH-1000XM6 28 out of 30 for noise cancelling, just behind the two Bose Ultras, and rates it the best of the standard wireless headphones for call quality thanks to extra microphones.

It also has the most useful extras: holding a hand over the earcup switches on transparency mode for a quick chat, and TechRadar finds the controls easier to use than Bose's. It has the more detailed, neutral sound of the big three.

Weighs about 254 g

TechRadar lists a $449 list price

products.name: Bose QuietComfort Headphones
why: TechRadar scored these only a couple of points below far pricier models, including Bose's own Ultras, the Sony XM6 and the Sonos Ace, and even rated them above the AirPods Max in its weighted real-world tests.
They are light and comfortable, and TechRadar expects to see them near $200 in sales, which makes them its best-value pick under $250.

TechRadar lists a $349 list price and a $199 typical street price

products.name: Soundcore Space One Pro
why: Tom's Guide names it the best-value noise-cancelling headphones overall. Its tester says the ANC is the star for the price and blocks low rumbles on buses and trains as well as voices.
It sounds much better than you would expect at this price, with detailed treble and thumping bass, and the soft ear cups stay comfortable for long sessions.

products.name: 1More SonoFlow Pro HQ51
why: TechRadar's pick for the best budget-friendly noise-cancelling headphones. In its tests the ANC matched the Sony XM4 and Cambridge Audio P100 SE, both more than twice the price, and it holds up well against high-pitched noise and voices.
It has a full mid-range, controlled bass and a folding design with a case included. Tom's Guide has also recommended an earlier SonoFlow Pro as its budget ANC pick.

products.name: Marshall Monitor III A.N.C.
why: Tom's Guide's pick for the best battery life it has seen: 70 hours with noise cancelling on and 100 hours with it off, and its testing got close to those numbers.
They are also among the most comfortable headphones its reviewer has worn, very light with soft foam pads, and they sound very good with Marshall's bass-and-treble tuning.

products.name: Bowers & Wilkins PX7 S3
why: Tom's Guide gives these its best-sound award, saying the audio beats even the AirPods Max, with impactful but balanced bass, great mids and clear highs. Its reviewer found them more comfortable than the Bose QuietComfort Ultra over long sessions.

TechRadar agrees they have the best sound at this price, well ahead of the Sony, but says the noise cancelling is clearly a step below the Bose, Sony and Sonos models, which is why they did not enter its ANC contest.

tips.title: How to choose
items: If you want the most silence, buy a Bose QuietComfort Ultra. If you want the best sound, look at the B&W PX7 S3 or the Sony.
Both outlets say around 30 hours is the norm for flagships. The Marshall and 1More last far longer, while the Bose Ultra first gen and Bose QuietComfort manage 24 hours.
TechRadar says the Bose QuietComfort Ultra often drops to about $300 and the Bose QuietComfort to about $200, so avoid paying full list price.
TechRadar's audiologist says ANC lets you listen at a lower volume. Keep it to about 60 percent volume for no more than 60 minutes at a time.

faq: Which noise-cancelling headphones are best overall?
Tom's Guide picks the Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2nd Gen) and TechRadar scored them joint best for noise cancelling in its tests.
What is the best cheap pair?
TechRadar's best under $100 is the 1More SonoFlow Pro HQ51. Tom's Guide's best under $100 is the JLab JBuds Lux ANC, a $79 list-price pair with up to 40 hours of ANC battery.
Are the Sonos Ace Ultra worth considering?
Tom's Guide names the Sonos Ace Ultra its best alternative. Its ANC is a big upgrade, solidly above Sony and only slightly behind Bose, but at $449 it mainly makes sense if you own Sonos speakers.
Do noise-cancelling headphones replace hearing protection?
No. TechRadar's audiologist says ANC headphones are not hearing protection and are no substitute at concerts, shooting ranges or around power tools.
